mainTopic: Conflicting witnesses (תרי ותרי) about a husband's death, a divorce, or a betrothal, and whether a woman who remarried must leave.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier rule: a woman who gives a sensible excuse (אמתלא) for changing her claim is believed. Even so, שמואל, who reviewed this rule forty times, would not rely on it for himself. Next a ברייתא discusses two witnesses against two (תרי ותרי) about whether a husband died or whether a woman was divorced. She may not remarry, but if she did, the תנא קמא says she stays and רבי מנחם בר יוסי says she must leave. The גמרא asks how she can stay when the couple faces an אשם תלוי. It answers that she married one of her own witnesses and she says 'בָּרִי לִי'. רבי יוחנן then rules that after the fact she stays in the death case but must leave in the divorce case. The גמרא gives three explanations: אביי (one witness against one, and a death witness counts as two), רבא (in divorce she can contradict her husband), and רב אסי (the witnesses said 'just now,' so a divorce can be checked by asking for the גט). The amud ends with a ברייתא contrasting split testimony about betrothal, where she stays, with split testimony about divorce, where she must leave.

steps.title: Her excuse makes her believed
steps.stepSummary: The earlier ruling ends: if the woman gives a believable excuse (אמתלא) for her first statement, she is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she gives a reason for what she said before, she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that began before this section: a woman who changed her story is believed if she explains why she said the first thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once someone says something, she cannot take it back. An אמתלא is a sensible explanation for why she said the first thing, and it allows her new claim to be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: A believable excuse or reason explaining an earlier statement

phrases.english: [If she gives] a reason for her words, she is believed.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started earlier, about a woman who first said she was married and then said she was not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ruling discussed just before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An אמתלא lets a woman's changed claim be believed.

steps.title: שמואל learned it forty times but did not rely on it himself
steps.stepSummary: שמואל went over this rule forty times, yet he still would not act on it in his own life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learned it from him forty times, and even so שמואל did not act on it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how seriously שמואל took this rule, and how carefully he behaved even so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reviewing the rule forty times shows that שמואל knew the law well. Even so, he would not rely on this lenient ruling in his own personal case. He was being extra careful for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: An action, acting on a ruling in practice
For himself, in his own life

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person may be stricter with himself than the law requires, even when he knows the law well.

phrases.english: He learned it from him forty times,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא עֲבַד שְׁמוּאֵל עוֹבָדָא בְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: and even so, Shmuel did not act on it for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about how שמואל treated the ruling from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even though the rule is lenient, שמואל did not rely on it for himself.

steps.title: Two witnesses against two: she may not remarry
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: when two witnesses say the husband died (or that she was divorced) and two say he did not, she may not remarry. If she did remarry, the תנא קמא says she stays, and רבי מנחם בר יוסי says she must leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: two say 'he died' and two say 'he did not die'; or two say 'she was divorced' and two say 'she was not divorced'. She may not remarry, and if she remarried she does not leave. רבי מנחם בר יוסי says: she leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about two pairs of witnesses who contradict each other about a woman's status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two pairs of witnesses cancel each other out, so we are left in doubt. Because of the doubt, she should not remarry at the start. The argument is over what happens after she already remarried: the תנא קמא leaves her with the new husband, while רבי מנחם בר יוסי makes her leave.

keyTerms.meaning: She may not marry (at the start)
She does not have to leave (her new husband)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate questions here: may she remarry at the start (no), and must she leave if she already did (this is where they argue). Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Two say 'he died,' and two say 'he did not die.'
Two say 'she was divorced,' and two say 'she was not divorced':
this woman may not remarry,
and if she remarried, she does not leave.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: תֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Menachem bar Yosei says: she leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two witnesses against two she may not remarry. If she remarried, the תנא קמא says she stays and רבי מנחם בר יוסי says she leaves.

steps.title: רבי מנחם בר יוסי limits his ruling to when the witnesses came first
steps.stepSummary: רבי מנחם בר יוסי explains that she must leave only if the contradicting witnesses came before she remarried. If she remarried first and then they came, she stays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מנחם בר יוסי said: When do I say she leaves? When the witnesses came and afterward she remarried. But if she remarried and afterward the witnesses came, she does not leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מנחם בר יוסי narrows his own opinion so we know exactly when he says she must leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of events matters. If she married knowing there were witnesses against her, she did wrong and must leave. If she married properly and only later did the opposing witnesses show up, they are not enough to break up the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: At a time when, in a case where

phrases.english: Rabbi Menachem bar Yosei said:
When do I say she leaves?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבָּאוּ עֵדִים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִשֵּׂאת.
phrases.english: When witnesses came, and afterward she remarried.
phrases.notes: These are the witnesses who say she is still married.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִשֵּׂאת וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים — לֹא תֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: But if she remarried and afterward witnesses came, she does not leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי מנחם בר יוסי's opinion from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She leaves only if the opposing witnesses came before she remarried.

steps.title: But the new husband is in doubt and needs an אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since it is two against two, the man who lives with her is in a doubtful sin and would need an אשם תלוי. So how can she stay?
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, it is two against two! The man who lives with her stands to bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling that she may stay with her new husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two against two leaves a real doubt about whether she is still married. A doubt about a sin like this obligates an אשם תלוי. So it seems impossible to let the marriage continue.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'suspended' guilt-offering brought for a possible sin
The man who lives with her

phrases.english: After all, it is two against two,
the one who lives with her stands to bring an asham talui!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling 'if she remarried she does not leave'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that she may stay with her new husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two against two creates a real doubt, and a doubtful sin of this kind needs an אשם תלוי. So the marriage should not be allowed to continue.

steps.title: רב ששת: she married one of her own witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that she married one of the witnesses who said she is free, so for him there is no doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: For example, where she married one of her witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by pointing to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new husband himself testified that she is free. In his own mind there is no doubt, so he does not need an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as in a case where
From her witnesses (the ones who said she is free)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
For example, where she married one of her witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְאֶחָד מֵעֵדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the ruling in a narrow case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The new husband is in doubt, like anyone else.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband is one of the witnesses, so he is sure and has no doubt.

steps.title: But she herself is in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if the husband is sure, the woman herself is still in doubt and would need an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: She herself stands to bring an אשם תלוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's answer only removes the doubt for the husband. The woman still has the same doubt as before, so the original problem remains for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands, is in the position of

phrases.english: She herself stands to bring an asham talui!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's answer that she married one of her witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the husband's doubt is removed. The woman is still in doubt and would need an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: She says 'I am sure'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is where she says 'בָּרִי לִי', meaning she is certain, so she has no doubt either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where she says: 'It is clear to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer: the woman herself claims to know for sure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is sure that her husband died or that she was divorced, then she is not in doubt. Now neither she nor her new husband needs an אשם תלוי, so they may stay married.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear to me, I am sure

steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא, she may stay married only when both sides are sure: the husband is one of her witnesses, and she says 'בָּרִי לִי'.

phrases.english: Where she says: 'It is clear to me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman is unsure and would need an אשם תלוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: She says she is sure, so she has no doubt either.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the death case and the divorce case are different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that in both cases she may not remarry. But if she did remarry, in the death case she stays, and in the divorce case she must leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Two say 'he died' and two say 'he did not die': she may not remarry, and if she remarried she does not leave. Two say 'she was divorced' and two say 'she was not divorced': she may not remarry, and if she remarried she leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his own ruling, and he treats the death case differently from the divorce case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treated both cases the same. רבי יוחנן separates them: after the fact, a remarriage is allowed to stand in the death case but not in the divorce case. The next step asks why, and steps 11–18 give the answers of אביי, רבא and רב אסי.
steps.confusionAlert: Read the endings carefully: in the death case it says 'לֹא תֵּצֵא' (she does not leave), and in the divorce case it says 'תֵּצֵא' (she leaves).
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the next question: why should a divorce doubt be stricter than a death doubt?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Two say 'he died,' and two say 'he did not die':

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זוֹ לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא, וְאִם נִשֵּׂאת — לֹא תֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: this woman may not remarry, and if she remarried, she does not leave.
Two say 'she was divorced,' and two say 'she was not divorced':

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זוֹ לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא, וְאִם נִשֵּׂאת — תֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: this woman may not remarry, and if she remarried, she leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling that treats the two cases of the ברייתא in step 3 differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a two-against-two doubt she may not remarry. After the fact, she stays in the death case but must leave in the divorce case.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן lets her stay in the death case but makes her leave in the divorce case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes the first case (death) different from the second case (divorce)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן gave different results for death and divorce. This question sets up the answers that come next, from אביי, רבא and רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the testimony conflicts, so you would expect the same result. Yet רבי יוחנן says that once she remarried, she stays in the death case and leaves in the divorce case. The גמרא wants the reason for that difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part (here, the death case)
The last part (here, the divorce case)

phrases.english: What is different about the first part
phrases.notes: The first part is רבי יוחנן's death case from the last step, where she may stay.

phrases.english: and what is different about the last part?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the split ruling of רבי יוחנן in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the death case and the divorce case end differently after she remarries.

steps.title: אביי: In the death case, one witness counts as two
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the case involves single witnesses. One witness who says the husband died is believed like two, so the one who says he is alive is outweighed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Read the case as one witness against one witness. When one witness says 'he died,' the Rabbis believed him as if he were two witnesses. This follows עולא, who said that wherever the Torah believes one witness, he counts as two. So the witness who says 'he did not die' is only one, and one witness cannot stand against two.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that רבי יוחנן was talking about one witness against one witness, not two against two. In the death case, the witness who says the husband died gets the strength of two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one against one would be a tie. But the Rabbis gave special belief to a single witness who reports a husband's death, and עולא says such a witness counts as two. So it is really 'two' against one, and the opposing witness loses. That is why she may stay.

keyTerms.term: אֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: One person's words are worth nothing against two

phrases.english: אביי said:
Explain it as a case of one witness.
One witness says, "He died,"
the Rabbis believed him like two witnesses,
and this follows עולא.
For עולא said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah believed one witness,
he counts here as two.
And this one who says, "He did not die,"
is just one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: and the words of one are worth nothing against two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 for the death case by redefining the case as one witness against one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case involves single witnesses. The witness who says the husband died counts as two (following עולא), so the opposing single witness is outweighed and she may stay.

steps.title: Then she should be allowed to remarry from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: if it is really two against one, why not let her remarry even from the beginning?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, she should be allowed to remarry even from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי. If the witness for death really counts as two, why did רבי יוחנן say she should not remarry in the first place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said 'she should not remarry, but if she did, she stays.' אביי's explanation makes the death side clearly stronger, which seems to permit remarriage right away. So the first half of רבי יוחנן's ruling now looks unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, before the act

phrases.english: If so,
she should be allowed even from the start!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the death witness counts as two.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the side saying 'he died' is legally stronger, there should be no reason to stop her from remarrying even at the start, yet רבי יוחנן said she should not.

steps.title: Because of רב אסי: keep away from questionable situations
steps.stepSummary: The answer: she should still not remarry at the start, because רב אסי teaches that a person should stay away from things that look crooked or questionable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of רב אסי. For רב אסי said: 'Remove from yourself a crooked mouth, and put devious lips far away from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that she is technically allowed. But because there is a witness against her, it looks bad, so we tell her not to remarry at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against remarrying at the start is not a real prohibition. It comes from רב אסי's teaching to keep away from anything that seems improper. Since this concern applies only before the fact, once she has remarried she does not have to leave.

phrases.english: It is because of רב אסי.
For רב אסי said:
"Remove from yourself a crooked mouth,
and put devious lips far away from you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason: the rule against remarrying at the start is a matter of keeping away from impropriety, not a true prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the death side is stronger, she may remarry even at the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strictly she may, but because of רב אסי's teaching she should avoid it at the start. After the fact, she stays.

steps.title: אביי: In the divorce case, both witnesses agree she was married
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the divorce case. Both witnesses agree she was a married woman, so the lone witness who says she was divorced is outweighed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part: one witness says 'she was divorced,' and one witness says 'she was not divorced.' Both of them are testifying that she was a married woman. So the one who says 'she was divorced' is only one, and one witness cannot stand against two.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now explains the second case, the divorce case, using the same one-against-one setup. Here the result flips, and she must leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness who says she was divorced still admits she was married before that. So both witnesses agree she was once married, and only one claims a divorce. Unlike the death case, no special rule makes a divorce witness count as two, so he loses and she must leave.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the case is one witness against one. A death witness counts as two, so she stays. In divorce, both witnesses agree she was married, so the single divorce witness loses and she must leave.

phrases.english: The last part:
one witness says, "She was divorced,"
and one witness says, "She was not divorced,"
both of them are testifying that she was a married woman.
And this one who says "she was divorced"
is just one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: and the words of one are worth nothing against two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer from step 11 by explaining the divorce case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In divorce, both witnesses confirm she was married, and only one claims a divorce. The single witness loses, so she must leave.

steps.title: רבא: It is two against two, and divorce is different because she can argue
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the case really is two witnesses against two. רבי יוחנן agreed with רבי מנחם בר יוסי that she must leave only in divorce, because there she can argue with her husband, but in death she cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really it is two witnesses against two. רבי יוחנן agreed with רבי מנחם בר יוסי in the case of divorce, but not in the case of death. What is the reason? In death, she cannot contradict him. In divorce, she can contradict him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from אביי. He keeps the case as two against two and explains the difference by how the woman behaves in each situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מנחם בר יוסי held that even after remarrying she must leave. If a 'dead' husband shows up alive, there is nothing to argue, so a woman would be very careful before remarrying. Her remarriage shows she is sure, and she may stay. If a husband says he never divorced her, she can argue back, so she might take a risk. That is why רבי יוחנן agreed with רבי מנחם בר יוסי only for divorce and makes her leave.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: אביי says one witness against one, where a death witness counts as two. רבא says two against two, and divorce is stricter because a woman can argue with her husband about a divorce, but cannot argue that a living husband is dead.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not disagreeing with the outcome. Both אביי and רבא agree she stays in the death case and leaves in the divorce case. They only disagree about why.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Really, it is two witnesses against two.
And רבי יוחנן agreed with

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בַּר יוֹסֵי בְּגֵרוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: the words of רבי מנחם בר יוסי in the case of divorce,
but did not agree in the case of death.
What is the reason?
Death: she cannot contradict him,
Divorce: she can contradict him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם תְּרֵי וּתְרֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 10, rejecting אביי's one-witness setup.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is two against two. רבי יוחנן follows רבי מנחם בר יוסי (she must leave) only for divorce. In death she cannot deny a returning husband, so she is careful and her remarriage is trusted. In divorce she can deny his claim, so her remarriage is suspect.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the גמרא weighs how likely a person is to act carefully, and not only the count of witnesses, when deciding the outcome after the fact.

steps.title: Would a woman really be that bold in front of her husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's explanation from רב המנונא's rule that a woman does not lie brazenly to her husband's face.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a woman really that bold? Didn't רב המנונא say that a woman who tells her husband 'You divorced me' is believed? We assume a woman would not be so brazen as to lie to her husband's face!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer from the previous step. רבא said that in a divorce case the woman can argue with her husband, but רב המנונא says a woman would never brazenly lie to her husband's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer pictures the woman standing up to her husband and claiming he divorced her. רב המנונא says the opposite: a woman is not brazen in front of her husband, which is why she is even believed when she says 'you divorced me.' So how could רבא picture her boldly arguing with him?

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא whose rule is quoted here
a presumption, a default assumption about how people act

steps.confusionAlert: רב המנונא's rule actually helps the woman: she is believed because we assume she would not lie to her husband's face. The גמרא is using that same assumption to question רבא's picture of her arguing with him.

phrases.english: And is she so bold, to that extent?
phrases.notes: "She" is the woman in רבא's case, who would argue with her husband that he divorced her.

phrases.english: But didn't רב המנונא say:
A woman who said to her husband
"You divorced me" is believed.
There is a presumption that a woman is not brazen
to her husband's face!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי חֲצִיפָה כּוּלֵּי הַאי? וְהָאָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reasoning from step 15 that in divorce she can argue with her husband.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that in a divorce case the woman will argue with her husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב המנונא assumes a woman is not brazen to her husband's face, so it seems she would not argue a false claim in front of him.

steps.title: With witnesses backing her, she would be bold
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא's rule applies only when no witnesses support her. When witnesses back her up, she would certainly be bold.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule only applies when there are no witnesses supporting her. But when there are witnesses supporting her, she will certainly be bold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting רב המנונא's rule. A woman alone won't lie to her husband's face, but with witnesses on her side she will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case there are two witnesses who say she was divorced. That support gives her the confidence to stand up to her husband, so רב המנונא's assumption does not apply. This saves רבא's explanation.

phrases.english: This applies only where
there are no witnesses supporting her,
but where there are witnesses
who support her,
she will certainly be brazen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A woman is never brazen enough to contradict her husband to his face.
steps.terutzMaskana: She avoids being brazen only when she stands alone. With supporting witnesses she will contradict him, so רבא's explanation stands.

steps.title: רב אסי: the witnesses said it happened just now
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי explains רבי יוחנן's distinction differently. The witnesses said 'he died now' or 'he divorced her now.' A death cannot be checked right away, but a divorce can, by asking her to show the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: the case is where the witnesses said 'he died just now' or 'he divorced her just now.' A death can't be checked right away. A divorce can be checked, because we tell her: if that's really what happened, show us your גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי offers a different explanation of why רבי יוחנן treats divorce more strictly than death. The difference is that a divorce can be checked on the spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the witnesses said the divorce happened just now, she should have the גט in hand and cannot easily claim she lost it. If she cannot show it, the witnesses who said she was divorced look false, so even if she remarried she must leave. With 'he died now' there is no quick way to check, so the doubt stays and she does not have to leave.

keyTerms.meaning: to clarify it, to check it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of why רבי יוחנן treats divorce more strictly than death. אביי says it is one witness against one, and a death witness counts as two. רבא says it is two against two, and in divorce she can contradict her husband, so her remarrying is suspect. רב אסי says the witnesses said it happened 'now,' and a divorce can be checked by asking for the גט.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same teaching of רב אסי quoted in step 13 about staying away from crooked things. Here רב אסי gives a new answer that stands as an alternative to רבא's.

phrases.english: רב אסי said:
For example, where the witnesses say
"He died just now," or "He divorced her just now."
A death has no way to be checked.
A divorce has a way to be checked,
since we say to her:
If it is true that this is what happened,
show us your גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּאָמְרִי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation from רבא's (step 15) for רבי יוחנן's distinction between death and divorce.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי יוחנן say she must leave only in a divorce case and not in a death case?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The witnesses said it happened just now. A divorce can be checked right away by asking for the גט, but a death cannot.

steps.title: Two against two about betrothal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if two witnesses say she was betrothed and two say she was not, she should not marry, but if she already married she does not have to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if two witnesses say she was betrothed and two say she was not, she should not marry. But if she did marry, she does not have to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about two witnesses against two. This first half is about whether she was ever betrothed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the witnesses are evenly split, she is told not to marry from the start. After the fact, though, we do not force her out of her marriage. The ברייתא does not give its reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: she does not have to leave her husband

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Two witnesses say, "She was betrothed,"
and two say, "She was not betrothed":
this woman should not marry,
and if she married, she does not have to leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on the related topic of two witnesses against two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Split testimony about betrothal: she should not marry from the start, but after the fact she stays married.

steps.title: Two against two about divorce
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if two say she was divorced and two say she was not, she should not remarry, and if she did, she must leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two witnesses say she was divorced and two say she was not, she should not remarry. And if she did remarry, she must leave.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the same ברייתא. Here the witnesses argue about a divorce, and the ruling is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both halves start the same way: she should not marry. The difference is after the fact. In the betrothal case she stays, but in the divorce case she must leave her new husband. The ברייתא states this difference without explaining it yet.
steps.whatToRemember: Betrothal dispute: if she married, she stays. Divorce dispute: if she married, she must leave. Compare the two halves of the ברייתא side by side.
steps.confusionAlert: The first line of both halves is the same ('she should not marry'). The difference is only in the last word: לֹא תֵּצֵא (she stays) versus תֵּצֵא (she must leave).

phrases.english: Two witnesses say, "She was divorced,"
and two say, "She was not divorced":
this woman should not remarry,
and if she remarried, she must leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים נִתְגָּרְשָׁה וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים לֹא נִתְגָּרְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the parallel divorce case, which gets a stricter outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Split testimony about divorce: she should not remarry, and if she did, she must leave.
